summary: The Organization menu entry does not open a page of its own. It opens the same page as the Preferences dashboard icon.

approvedExpectation.designConstraint: Arrival is asserted on page content, never on the address, because the Organization entry shares /ssweb/setup/prefs/preferences.eo with the Preferences dashboard icon.

observedBehaviour.method: page.getByRole('heading') filtered by isVisible() - the same ARIA role engine that expect(getByRole(...)) uses. Deliberately NOT a querySelector over h1,h2,h3,legend,caption, which produced a false result on this application once before and cost three scenarios.

comparison.sameMainTextNote: The full visible text differs somewhere beyond the shared opening. That difference has NOT been shown to be a stable discriminator - it may be a list of organization names or another volatile value - so it is not used as one. Asserting on an unexamined difference would be a guess wearing the clothes of evidence.

viaVaultMenuEntry.note: Vault IS a distinct destination on every measure. Only the Organization half of AC-ETA-411-006 is in question.

consequence: TS-ETA-411-005 asserts that the Organization entry opens the organization administration settings, which it demonstrably does. It cannot assert that Organization is a destination distinct from Preferences, because on this evidence it is not. No approved artifact has been edited and no assertion has been quietly weakened to make the scenario pass.
notResolvedBecause: Whether AC-ETA-411-006 intends 'their own pages' to mean two distinct destinations, or simply that each entry opens the settings it names, is a statement about what the product should do. An agent may not decide it. AMB-ETA-411-006 asked a narrower version of this question and was left REVIEW_REQUIRED.
options: Accept that Organization and Preferences are two routes to one page, and record AC-ETA-411-006 as covered by the assertion actually made.
Treat the shared destination as an application defect and file it, leaving AC-ETA-411-006 uncovered until it is fixed.
Re-word AC-ETA-411-006 at Gate 1, which returns ETA-411 to the AC_APPROVAL gate with a new artifactVersion.
